title: Private Service Edge software and deployment steps by platform
aliases: private service edge software by platform

prose.text: {{software-by-platform}} The About page's STIG list [[zpa.private-service-edges.deployment:stig-images]] differs from the Linux guide's and the software page's on Nutanix {{divergence:stig-images-nutanix}}, and its platform list [[zpa.private-service-edges.deployment:supported-platforms]] differs from the software page's {{divergence:platform-list-nutanix}}.

prose.label: Linux and RPM.
prose.text: {{linux-rpm}} The Linux guide names two repositories for RHEL 9 {{divergence:yum-repository}}.

prose.label: Google Cloud Platform.
prose.text: {{gcp}} The GCP firewall step names the Private Cloud Controller {{gap:gcp-firewall-wording}}.

prose.label: Docker.
prose.text: {{docker}} The procedures' memory and processor values sit below the recommended sizing table [[zpa.private-service-edges.deployment:sizing-table]] {{divergence:minimum-resources}}. The software page lists no Kubernetes or OpenShift image for Private Service Edges {{gap:pse-containers}}.

Capacity, the host OS and limits are in [[zpa.private-service-edges.deployment]] and enrollment in [[zpa.private-service-edges.enrollment]]. The Private Cloud Controller's equivalent is [[zpa.private-service-edges.private-cloud-controller.deployment]].

linux-rpm.statement: The Linux guide's repository definition uses baseurl https://yum.private.zscaler.com/yum/el9 with gpgcheck=1, and for RHEL 8-based deployments the baseurl must be https://yum.private.zscaler.com/yum/el8. The console asks for confirmation twice and the GPG fingerprint should match a6fe 2422 fce7 e8ac 672e 9e51 644e a315 8765 e1dd. If the Private Service Edge cannot download the RPM package, the guide has the package downloaded on a server, chmod 777 applied to zpa-service-edge.rpm, yum localinstall run, and iptables -I INPUT 1 -j ACCEPT run.

quotes: [zscaler] name=Zscaler Private Access Repository baseurl=https://yum.private.zscaler.com/yum/el9 enabled=1 gpgcheck=1 gpgkey=https://yum.private.zscaler.com/yum/el9/gpg
For Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8-based deployments, you must use https://yum.private.zscaler.com/yum/el8 as the baseurl.
The Private Service Edge console asks for confirmation twice. Enter y both times and ensure that the GPG fingerprint matches, a6fe 2422 fce7 e8ac 672e 9e51 644e a315 8765 e1dd
If the Private Service Edge can't download the RPM package, you must download the package on a server:
$ chmod 777 zpa-service-edge.rpm
$ sudo yum localinstall zpa-service-edge.rpm
$ iptables -I INPUT 1 -j ACCEPT

aws.statement: The AWS guide says Private Service Edges must be deployed in the customer's VPCs, with a pair deployed for each VPC for resilience and scalability, and that they should be deployed across Availability Zones. Their security groups should accept incoming connections from Client Connector and App Connectors and permit inbound and outbound access on port 443, and allow inbound SSH. The AMI is currently available under Community AMIs for us-west-2 and us-east-1, with other regions requested through Zscaler Support, and if IMDSv2 is enabled the Private Service Edges will fetch the AWS VM ID.

quotes: For AWS, you must deploy Private Service Edges in your Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs). For each VPC, there should be a pair of Private Service Edges deployed for resilience and scalability.

Private Service Edges should be in appropriate security groups to accept incoming connections from Zscaler Client Connector and App Connectors. The Private Service Edges' security group should permit inbound and outbound access on port 443. The security group should allow inbound SSH to the AWS EC2 instance.

The Private Service Edge AMI is currently available under Community AMIs for regions US West (Oregon) - us-west-2 and US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1. If you require an AMI in another region, you can request this through Zscaler Support.
The Private Service Edges should be deployed across Availability Zones to ensure continuity of service in the event of an incident.
If Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) is enabled, Private Service Edges will fetch the AWS VM ID.

aws-auto-scaling.statement: In the AWS guide's auto scaling steps the AMI is filtered for zpa-service-edge-2025.12, the security group's Inbound tab allows access to the public IP address on port 443, the group size is 2 and the target value is 50. The guide says each Private Service Edge is capable of passing 400 to 500 Mbps traffic, and that OAuth 2.0 enrollment is unavailable with Auto Scaling.

quotes: From the AMI menu, filter for zpa-service-edge-2025.12 and select it from the list.
On the Inbound tab, allow access to the public IP address on port 443.
Group size: Enter 2.
Target value: Enter 50.
each Private Service Edge is capable of passing 400 to 500 Mbps traffic.
OAuth 2.0 enrollment is unavailable with Auto Scaling.

azure.statement: The Azure guide has the reader search for Red Hat and select a RHEL 9.x that meets the requirements in the prerequisites, create a rule allowing inbound SSH connections for port 22 and HTTPS connections for port 443 and one allowing outbound connections for port 443, and disable inbound access on port 22 for the security group associated with the Private Service Edge in Azure.

quotes: Search for Red Hat Linx and select a RHEL 9.x that meets the requirements in the prerequisites.
Create a rule that allows inbound SSH connections for port 22 and HTTPS connections for port 443.
Create a rule that allows outbound connections for port 443.
In Azure, make sure you disable inbound access on port 22 for the security group associated with the Private Service Edge.

gcp.statement: The GCP guide says for each VPC there must be at least a pair of Private Service Edges, and that they should be deployed across regions and zones. Zscaler recommends the n2-standard-4 or n2-highcpu-4 machine types, and n2-highcpu-4 is given as 4 vCPU, 2 core and 4 GB memory. Its autoscaling steps select a minimum and maximum of 2 and 4 instances, enter 80 in the Target CPU utilization field and 300 in the Initialization period field.

quotes: For each VPC there must be at least a pair of Private Service Edges deployed for resilience and scalability.
The Private Service Edges should be deployed across regions and zones to ensure continuity of service in the event of an incident.
Zscaler recommends using the n2-standard-4 or n2-highcpu-4 machine types:
n2-highcpu-4: The supported specifications are 4 vCPU, 2 core, and 4 GB memory.
Select a minimum and maximum number of instances as 2 and 4, respectively.
Enter 80 in the Target CPU utilization field.
Enter 300 in the Initialization period field.

hyper-v.statement: The Hyper-V guide uses the VHDX https://dist.private.zscaler.com/vms/Azure/2026.09/zpa-service-edge-el9-2026.09.vhdx, selects Generation 1, enters 4096 for startup memory and enters 2 for the number of virtual processors.

quotes: https://dist.private.zscaler.com/vms/Azure/2026.09/zpa-service-edge-el9-2026.09.vhdx
On the Specify Generation page, select Generation 1, then click Next.
Startup memory: Enter 4096 for the amount of memory to use when starting up the virtual machine.
Click Processor, and enter 2 for the number of virtual processors.

nutanix.statement: The Nutanix AHV guide uses the image URL https://dist.private.zscaler.com/vms/VMware/2026.07/zpa-service-edge-el9-2026.07.ova, has the VMDK file extracted from the OVA, selects DISK as the Image Type, requires a minimum of 4 for Number Of Cores Per vCPU, and runs systemctl daemon-reload and systemctl start zpa-service-edge.

quotes: https://dist.private.zscaler.com/vms/VMware/2026.07/zpa-service-edge-el9-2026.07.ova
Extract the VMDK file from the OVA.
Image Type: Select DISK from the drop-down menu.
Number Of Cores Per vCPU: Enter the number of cores for the virtual CPU. The minimum required value is 4.
$ systemctl daemon-reload $ systemctl start zpa-service-edge

RHEL 9 deployments are only supported on ESXi 7.0 Update 2 or later.

docker.statement: The Private Service Edge Docker image is available on Docker Hub for both the AMD64 and ARM64 platforms and requires an environment variable named ZPA_PROVISION_KEY. A Publish IP must be configured in the Admin UI, a public IP address that receives requests for port 443 from clients and App Connectors, and Docker restarted afterwards with docker restart <container_name>. A minimum of 4 cores and 8 GB RAM is required for x86-64 systems, 2 cores and 4 GB RAM for ARM64 systems, and only one container per host is allowed.

quotes: The Private Service Edge for Private Access (ZPA) Docker image is available on Docker Hub for both the AMD64 and ARM64 platforms:
An environment variable named ZPA_PROVISION_KEY is required to run this image.
You must configure a Publish IP in the Admin UI. This public IP address receives requests for port 443 from clients and App Connectors when communicating with the Private Service Edge.
After the Publish IP is configured, restart Docker using the command: docker restart <container_name>.
A minimum of 4 cores and 8 GB RAM is required for x86-64 systems.
A minimum of 2 cores and 4 GB RAM is required for ARM64 systems.
Only one container per host is allowed.

gcp-firewall-wording.title: The Private Service Edge GCP guide's firewall step names the Private Cloud Controller
gcp-firewall-wording.detail: The GCP guide's firewall step says the Private Cloud Controller must have ingress and egress on TCP port 22 and egress on TCP port 443, in a Private Service Edge guide. It gives no inbound TCP 443 rule, which a Private Service Edge accepts elsewhere in the graph (zpa.private-service-edges.data-path).

quotes: The Private Cloud Controller must have ingress and egress traffic directions on TCP port 22 for SSH, and egress traffic directions on TCP port 443 to reach Private Access.

pse-containers.title: Private Service Edges on Kubernetes or OpenShift
pse-containers.detail: The software page lists Docker but no Kubernetes or OpenShift image for Private Service Edges, and no captured Private Service Edge Kubernetes guide exists. This is an absence in the captures, not a statement that they are unsupported.
